Harm: this is exactly the shape the 2026-09-05 addendum names (Antti: "traces of what should not exist and we say that should not exist. chasing phantoms") — a present-tense sentence whose subject is a thing that does not exist ("No … tail"), no transition verb, so the pre-existing tense test would have missed it. git diff c0c37913..HEAD on this file shows this exact clause was JUST rewritten from a transition-verb violation ("the tail that first shipped with it was cut as NVA, since…") into this phantom-negation form — the escalation ladder the rule itself warns against ("annotate the decline → convert it to a negative constraint"), each rewrite feeling like progress. The positive fact is already stated in the same sentence ("ranking the four changes nothing the student does and the bullet already shows the cost"), so per the rule's own second question ("is the positive fact already stated nearby?") the honest edit is deletion, not restatement. Harm is real but confined below the maintainer fence (no student ever reads it) — a future maintainer/judge re-derives a ghost that no longer exists.
